items.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022
items.q: one of the sessions that I mentioned to you where I wrote some music for Giovanni Hidalgo

ctx.x: For me the hardest part is usually coming up with a form and a chord sequence that’s not the twelve bar blues or something. And I wonder how do you go about finding an interesting and worthwhile set of changes?

Well most of the time I do write in either 16-bar phrases or, for Latin music it can be, you know 4-bar phrases or 8-bar phrases. There have been a few things that I’ve written that are in not the standard 4/4, 6/8 kind of rhythm. I generally don’t write in those rhythms but every now and then there’s an inspiration. I remember in particular writing a piece of a great percussionist Giovanni Hidalgo that was in 5/4, but it was — the melody statement was 5/4 but there was a little interlude that was in 4/4, and…
How do you charge for arrangements? Is there a union scale, sort of a minimum that you’re supposed to get and as you became more well known could your price for your charts adjust accordingly?
